item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is substantially closer to the frozen contract: it adds the exact Upload API, uses the established multipart helper, preserves FilesOption, validates inputs, and tests the required behavior. A introduces explicitly forbidden APIs and changes the required signature.","reasons":["B implements the exact required signature: Upload(ctx context.Context, fileName string, content io.Reader, opts ...FilesOption). A instead accepts ...UploadFileOption.","B directly reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile(\"file\", fileName, content), as required. A expands the helper with NewFileWithFields and uses that new machinery.","A adds association options and arbitrary multipart fields, despite the contract explicitly saying not to add association fields or change FilesOption behavior.","B tests multipart field name, filename, content, validation, source-reader errors, retry behavior, and an os.File body. A lacks a visible Upload source-reader-error test and spends substantial coverage on out-of-scope options and retry internals without satisfying the required API shape and scope constraints correctly."],"risks_a":["Upload does not have the contracted public signature and existing FilesOption values are no longer uniformly accepted.","Adds several new public option interfaces and association-field APIs explicitly prohibited by the contract.","Duplicates Add's request/response implementation instead of routing Upload through Add, while also introducing broad seekable-body retry machinery and altered closer semantics."],"risks_b":["Upload duplicates Add's option handling, request construction, decoding, and error checks instead of calling s.Files.Add as explicitly required.","The RawClient change globally buffers all non-native io.Reader bodies unless WithNoRetry is set, broadening scope and potentially causing unexpected memory use even when configured policy would not retry the request."]}
